LESSON: READING 12.4.1 PLAY: CHARACTERISATION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.4: Reading 12.4.1 Play: Characterisation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 12.4.1 Play: Characterisation. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Which words or expressions can you use to describe one’s character?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use the clues to describe the characters in a play
2. appreciate the role of characterisation in determining virtues and vices in the society

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 12.4.1 PLAY: CHARACTERISATION
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 12.4.1 Play: Characterisation helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 12.4.1 PLAY: CHARACTERISATION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Use the clues to describe the characters in a play

What this means
In this part you learn to use the clues to describe the characters in a play. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use the clues to describe the characters in a play.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 12.4.1 Play: Characterisation”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use the clues to describe the characters in a play. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate the role of characterisation in determining virtues and vices in the society

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of characterisation in determining virtues and vices in the society. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of characterisation in determining virtues and vices in the society.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 12.4.1 Play: Characterisation to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of characterisation in determining virtues and vices in the society. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 12.4.1 Play: Characterisation is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 12.4.1 Play: Characterisation”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: use the clues to describe the characters in a play)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 12.4.1 Play: Characterisation to a partner. (skill: appreciate the role of characterisation in determining virtues and vices in the society)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 12.4.1 Play: Characterisation to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: use the clues to describe the characters in a play.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of characterisation in determining virtues and vices in the society.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 12.4.1 Play: Characterisation from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 12.4.1 Play: Characterisation: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Reading 12.4.1 Play: Characterisation?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which words or expressions can you use to describe one’s character?
2. Why is characterisation important?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 12.4.1 Play: Characterisation means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: use the clues to describe the characters in a play.
5. Be able to: appreciate the role of characterisation in determining virtues and vices in the society.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
